plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-13 from the official Salem College 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (current edition, catoid=34), Psychological Science Major (BA) program page (poid=927). Salem College publishes major requirements but no official semester sequence for this program (its Print Degree Planner is a blank worksheet), so the plan is collected in requirements_only form as a single block. The recorded total (36) is the major requirement only: the catalog states a student must complete 10 courses (36 semester hours minimum) in psychology. The full BA degree requirements, including the Salem Impact core (published separately in the same catalog), are not itemized here. Per-course credits are the Hour(s) values printed on each course's own official course detail page in the same catalog; the program page itself prints no per-course credits. Fixed courses sum to 17. The five choice slots are recorded at exercised values summing to the printed 36 minimum (Knowledge Base elective 3, Statistics 4, Biology 4, Biological Foundations 4, Advanced Research Methods 4); catalog options whose printed credits differ from their slot's exercised value are disclosed on each slot: the Knowledge Base list also includes PSYC 180 Animal Behavior with Lab (4, with corequisite PSYC 180L) and PSYC 282 Special Topics in Psychology (1-4); the Statistics list also includes INTG 115 and PSYC 201 (3 each); the Advanced Research Methods list also includes PSYC 290 Honors Independent Study Psychological Science (3-4). A completion using lower-credit alternatives reaches the catalog's 36-hour minimum only through higher-credit choices elsewhere, as the catalog's minimum requires. PSYC 130 is cross-listed with SOCI 205. The Biology options carry corequisite labs BIOL 065L and BIOL 100L, which are separate lab courses not listed as program choices and are not placed. Course titles are the detail-page titles: PSYC 102 is titled Research Methods in Psychology on its detail page (the program structure heading groups it under Scientific Inquiry), and PSYC 350 is titled Senior Seminar on its detail page.

courses.title: Knowledge Base Elective
courses.choice_note: Choose one Knowledge Base elective. Options listed at the slot's exercised 3 credits: PSYC 110, PSYC 140, PSYC 150, PSYC 160, PSYC 190, PSYC 120 (all 3 Hour(s), prerequisite PSYC 010; PSYC 120 also accepts BIOL 065, BIOL 010 or BIOL 100). Also in the catalog list at different credits, disclosed not listed as options: PSYC 180 Animal Behavior with Lab (4 Hour(s), corequisite PSYC 180L, cross-listed BIOL 180) and PSYC 282 Special Topics in Psychology (1-4 Hour(s)).

courses.title: Statistics
courses.choice_note: Choose one Statistics course. Options listed at the slot's exercised 4 credits: BIOL 205 Biostatistics (4 Hour(s)) and MATH 107 Principles of Statistics (4 Hour(s)). Also in the catalog list at 3 credits, disclosed not listed as options: INTG 115 Introduction to Quantitative Reasoning (3 Hour(s)) and PSYC 201 Introduction to Psychological Statistics (3 Hour(s)).

courses.title: Biology
courses.choice_note: Choose one Biology course (catalog heading prints 'Chose one Biology'). Both options are 4 Hour(s) and carry a corequisite lab (BIOL 065L / BIOL 100L) that is a separate course not listed as a program choice.

courses.title: Biological Foundations
courses.choice_note: Choose one Biological Foundations course. All three options are 4 Hour(s). PSYC 230 and PSYC 240 require PSYC 102; PSYC 255 requires PSYC 102 or BIOL 100 (prerequisites as printed on the detail pages; recorded here, not in the slot prereq field, because the slot is a choice).

courses.title: Advanced Research Methods
courses.choice_note: Choose one Advanced Research Methods course (catalog heading prints 'Chose one Advanced Research Methods'). Option listed at the slot's exercised 4 credits: PSYC 220 Tests & Measurement (4 Hour(s); prerequisite PSYC 201 or MATH 107 or BIOL 205 or INTG 115, as printed). Also in the catalog list, disclosed not listed as an option: PSYC 290 Honors Independent Study Psychological Science (3-4 Hour(s), 3.5 GPA prerequisite, chair approval).
